clue.text: Exploit middle class

parts.note: M is a standard abbreviation for middle (as in medium, between small and large)
ilk means kind or class, as in 'people of that ilk'

explanation.surface: A call to take advantage of the middle class, perhaps through taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle class' reads as one social phrase, but it splits: M for middle, then ILK for class.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk someone or something is to drain every advantage from it, a figurative use of drawing milk from a cow.

clue.text: Spooner's male first aider reveals overall strategy

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, as Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: a sticking plaster is a first aid item
a man is a male

explanation.surface: A male paramedic is exposed as the brains behind a grand plan.
explanation.walkthrough: A first aider loosely stands for a plaster. Swap PL and M in PLASTER MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A master plan is a comprehensive scheme for achieving a large goal, an overall strategy.

clue.text: Brilliant escape by criminal

parts.note: on the lam is slang for escaping, so lam is an escape
bent is British slang for corrupt or criminal

explanation.surface: A clever getaway by a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent means softly glowing or flickering, and figuratively brilliant in wit or style.

clue.text: Random tests in place leading to arrests

parts.note: a spot is a place or location
to arrest is to check or halt, so arrests are checks

explanation.surface: Police conduct random tests at a location, which lead to people being arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot checks are inspections made without warning on a sample chosen at random.

clue.text: Pass instruction on how to make hair curl

definitions.meaning: a pass allowing entry or travel

definitions.text: instruction on how to make hair curl
definitions.meaning: read as two words, ... is an order to curl hair chemically

explanation.surface: A hairdressing manual gets approval for its curling guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit is an official document of permission, as is a pass.

clue.text: Regularly tied up, shot in the arm of German

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting with the first

parts.note: a shot in the arm is a boost, a tonic

explanation.surface: A German regularly tied up and given an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes T, E, U from TIED UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Teutonic describes the Teutons and, more broadly, anything characteristically German.

clue.text: Fruit with it?

explanation.surface: A trendy piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose hips are the red seed pods of roses, and hip is slang for trendy.

clue.text: My single bit of trivia: the knob on a deer's antler is a crown

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
one is a single unit

indicators.note: bit of takes a single letter from the start of trivia

explanation.surface: Someone shares a fun fact: the knob on a deer's antler is called a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of the clue is true trivia: a coronet is also the burr at the base of a deer's antler. It works as extra definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown, worn by peers and nobles below royalty.

clue.text: Help us love moderate

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal, popularly 'save our souls'
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A plea for help for those who love in moderation.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means middling or only fair, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Very fashionable and completely sane to collect silver

indicators.note: to collect means to take in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: all there is an idiom meaning fully in one's right mind
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A trendy and perfectly sensible person goes out to gather silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all the rage is extremely popular for the moment, a current craze.

clue.text: Relatively easy to smile coyly about learner driver

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the coy smile goes round the learner

parts.note: to simper is to smile in an affected, coy way
L is the learner driver's plate shown on British cars

explanation.surface: A driving examiner finds the test less demanding thanks to a shy smile from the learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpler is the comparative of simple, so it means easier by comparison with something else.

clue.text: Unionist politician's anger with southern judges

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: A Unionist MP's fury with judges from the south, a Northern Ireland political row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judges' could be a verb or a noun; here it is the plural noun for officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpires judge contests such as cricket matches, deciding disputed points as officials.

clue.text: Unusual Elgar concert inspires international modern music producer

indicators.note: inspires is read as breathes in, taking a letter inside
unusual tells us the letters of Elgar concert appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd Elgar concert prompts an international figure to create modern music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges ELGAR CONCERT, and 'inspires' puts I for international into the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric organ is an electronic keyboard instrument, a twentieth-century way of producing music.

clue.text: Try to offer Harry trees, but there aren't many here?

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
to bid is to offer a price

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so the letters of trees are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: An attempt to sell harried trees fails because hardly any grow in that place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' is the anagram signal, not a name. The definition leans on 'trees': there are few of them in this desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast desert across Mongolia and China, sparsely vegetated with scarcely any trees.

clue.text: Announced toffee-covered fruit possibilities

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so we want the word that sounds like the phrase

parts.note: candied dates are dates coated in sugar or toffee

explanation.surface: A confectioner reveals a range of sweet-coated fruit options.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates are those being considered for a role, the possible choices.

clue.text: Talk presented in short order

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: a pattern is an arrangement or order

explanation.surface: A speech delivered in a brief, orderly sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks the last letter, N, from PATTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Patter is rapid, glib speech, such as a salesman's or comedian's routine chat.

clue.text: Spies reported pancake mixture being used to make bread

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency

indicators.note: reported means said aloud, so we want a word that sounds like the one given

parts.note: batter is the mixture of flour, eggs and milk used for pancakes

explanation.surface: Secret agents say that pancake batter went into baking a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent BATTER sounds like the 'batta' ending of the bread's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciabatta is a flat Italian white loaf with a crisp crust and open texture.

clue.text: Scramble as the man blocks pincer movement

indicators.note: blocks means stands in the way, inside the other letters
movement says the letters of pincer are moved around

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A military man blocks an enemy's pincer manoeuvre by scrambling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pincer movement' looks like a military term, but 'movement' rearranges the letters to ENCIPR, which 'blocks' wraps round HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To encipher is to put a message into code, scrambling it so outsiders cannot read it.

clue.text: Inform a pretty accommodating Conservative

indicators.note: accommodating means housing or holding, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: quaint means attractively old-fashioned, pretty in a charming way

explanation.surface: Telling an attractive person that they are making room for a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone with something is to make them aware of it, to inform them.

clue.text: Former Queen Mother running inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within the word that follows

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
running means working or switched on

explanation.surface: The late Queen Mother jogging around inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Mother' reads as one royal title, but it splits into two separate pieces with 'running' placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Quondam is a Latin-derived adjective meaning that once was, former.

clue.text: Confused, walked like a duck with ducks

indicators.note: ducks is read as dodges out of the way, so the letter disappears

parts.note: to waddle is to walk with the rolling gait of a duck

explanation.surface: Bewildered, someone tottered along like a duck in the company of ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' looks like more birds but is the verb: W, short for with, ducks out of WADDLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled means muddled or confused, originally used of eggs gone bad.

clue.text: Academic lecturer made money

parts.note: earned means made money by work

explanation.surface: A university lecturer turned a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned describes scholarly people or works, showing deep academic knowledge.

clue.text: Fear of imitation ale, some might say

indicators.note: some might say means that in some pronunciations these words are spoken like the answer

parts.note: faux beer is fake ale

explanation.surface: Someone dreads fake beer, as some people put it.
explanation.definitionFit: A phobia is an intense, irrational dread of something.

clue.text: Not intend shag? That's that ruined!

definitions.text: Not intend shag? That's that ruined!

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the preceding words are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who did not mean to sleep with anyone laments that their plans are spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' rearranges NOT INTEND SHAG; the whole clue also describes the answer, an unplanned single encounter. Shag is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-night stand is a sexual encounter that is not intended to go any further than one occasion.

clue.text: National symbol of kingdom in West Indies, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A country's emblem from a Caribbean realm, at its origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kingdom in West Indies' looks like a place; take the first letter of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi, a flightless bird, is New Zealand's national emblem.

clue.text: After passing on power to replace American leader, becomes thorough

indicators.note: to replace means one letter is swapped in where the other was

parts.note: after someone has passed on, i.e. died, they are in death

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of the word American

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: After a death, power passes to a new American leader and things change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American leader' gives A, the first letter of American, which P replaces within IN DEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in depth is detailed and comprehensive, which is what thorough means.

clue.text: Dropping argument, starting late

indicators.note: starting late means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a row, having begun it too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like a verb, giving up the argument; it is a noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pat is a flat lump of dung, as in a cowpat.

clue.text: Prevent individual associated with Tory leader getting title

parts.note: to bar is to prevent or block
one is a single individual

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: Someone close to the Conservative leader is stopped from receiving an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British rank below a baron; the word names both the man and his rank.

clue.text: "Mum!" I announced loudly at first — after one minute, it's irrelevant

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come after one and minute in the answer

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
mater is Latin, and old British schoolboy slang, for mother

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letters of announced and loudly

explanation.surface: A child shouts 'Mum!' and a minute later declares it doesn't matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Announced loudly' looks like a homophone signal, but only the first letters A and L of those words are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Immaterial means of no importance or bearing on the matter in hand.

clue.text: That is finishing early one day a month

indicators.note: finishing early means the word stops short, losing its last letter

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Something finishes ahead of time on one particular date each month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishing early' cuts the final T from ID EST.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides fell on the 15th or 13th of each month.
